1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely from the server-side session via owner()/verified(); no user identifier is accepted from the request, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: Identity OTPs are hashed into the requesting session object and TOTP/recovery codes are hashed/encrypted per account, so a code cannot be replayed for another account.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/authenticator/confirm only mutates account flags; no other sessions in the sessions map are invalidated, so pre-existing sessions remain usable (only login rotates a session).

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (r.a.otp = await encrypt(secret)) and recovery codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: secureHex/bytes/randomFrom all use crypto.getRandomValues with modulo-bias rejection, and the AES key comes from crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie is used and the session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, though CSRF token and secrets do live in JS memory and are rendered into the page.

7.why: Server validates types and formats strictly: email regex plus length caps, six() for /^\d{6}$/, rec() for the ABCD-EFGH-IJKL pattern, and JSON body shape checking; storage is in-memory Maps so no SQL is involved.

8.why: All dynamic values (codes, secrets, error messages, log lines) are inserted with textContent; innerHTML is used only with static template markup, and a nonce-based CSP without 'unsafe-inline' backs this up.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all (all responses are JSON or the single HTML page), so there is no open-redirect surface, but equally no explicit allow-list mechanism exists.

10.why: headers() sets nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...'.

12.why: Server-side logging and error output are generic (fail() messages, catch-all 500), but the client deliberately writes the provisioning secret, otpauth URI, identity OTP, current TOTP and all backup codes to the browser console and an on-page 'Logs' panel.

13.why: Identity codes carry a used flag plus a 10-minute expiry, confirmed TOTP counters are recorded in acceptedTotpCounters to block replay, and recovery codes are deleted from the set on successful use with an expiry timestamp.

14.why: Login, identity verify, authenticator confirm and recovery verify all increment failure counters and impose a 5-minute lockout after 5 failures, returning 429.

15.why: Login deletes the pre-auth session and issues a fresh random 32-byte id (rotation), current() enforces a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie with Max-Age=0.
